name: Learn basic darts technique
blurb: A repeatable throw beats a strong one. Darts rewards consistency of stance, grip and release above everything else — and you can practise it in a hallway.
gear: A set of darts you like the feel of
A board mounted at regulation height, with the oche marked
steps: Set the board correctly: bullseye at 1.73 m, throwing line at 2.37 m. Practising at the wrong distance builds a useless groove.
Build a stance: side-on, front foot on the line, weight forward, body still.
Find a grip you can repeat and use exactly the same one on every dart.
Learn the throw: elbow up and fixed, only the forearm moves, and a full follow-through with the fingers pointing at the target.
Practise around the clock — hitting 1 through 20 in order — as a daily warm-up.
Learn the scoring and the standard checkouts, which is half the game at any social level.
tips: Moving the elbow or the body is the biggest source of inconsistency.
Aim at a specific wire or number segment, not at the board generally.
Throw smoothly. Power adds nothing and costs accuracy.
proof: You hit treble twenty regularly enough to average 45+ per three darts, and finish a game on a double.
